The methodology is framed as advisory design without target execution. The request to make clear that the methodology tests file read access and identifies the file objects being read is satisfied by the applicability statement for Linux file read access evaluation and by explicit prerequisites and evidence requirements referencing object identifier/path/permission state. No material unsupported factual claims or missing deliverables are identified.

interpretations.prerequisite_or_policy: Established policy source identified and documented specifying which process identities are authorized to read which objects under which conditions; policy reference and version recorded.
interpretations.legitimate_outcome: Policy is documented and the explicit read permission requirement for the object and mapping of identities to allowed/denied is recorded.
interpretations.distinguishing_control: Retrieve authoritative policy documentation/configuration or independently known authorization baseline for the object and record explicit read permission requirement and identity mapping.

interpretations.prerequisite_or_policy: Actual process identity resolution method known in principle, e.g., UID/GID, capabilities, SELinux/AppArmor context.
interpretations.legitimate_outcome: Identity attributes that will be used for comparison are recorded.
interpretations.distinguishing_control: Determine how actual process identity is resolved in the target environment and record the identity attributes used for comparison.

interpretations.prerequisite_or_policy: Policy states read is permitted for the test process identity for the identified object.
interpretations.legitimate_outcome: Access succeeds if policy permits and caller has read permission on the object. Source support: Linux open(2) requires caller have read permission on the object for read access.
interpretations.suspected_violation: No violation expected under allowed control.
interpretations.distinguishing_control: Allowed control configuration where policy permits read for chosen identity; evidence set includes process identity attributes, requested access mode, kernel return code/error message, timestamp and object identifier.

interpretations.prerequisite_or_policy: Policy states read is prohibited for the test process identity for the identified object.
interpretations.legitimate_outcome: Access is denied. Source support: Linux open(2) documents that requested access to the file is not allowed when permission is lacking.
interpretations.suspected_violation: No violation expected under denied control.
interpretations.distinguishing_control: Denied control configuration where policy prohibits read for chosen identity; same evidence set as allowed control collected for comparison.

interpretations.prerequisite_or_policy: Established policy with allowed and denied identities for a constant object.
interpretations.legitimate_outcome: Allowed identity + allowed control → success expected; denied identity + denied control → denial expected; cross combinations verify identity binding.
interpretations.suspected_violation: Outcome contradicts established policy for observed identity, e.g., denied identity succeeds or allowed identity is denied.
interpretations.distinguishing_control: Keep object and policy constant, vary process identity between allowed and denied identities; record divergence from expected outcomes as design artifact for future validation with evidence requirements.

Evidence notes – draft d64288cb04697

* Requirement coverage
  - requirement:method – draft describes reusable read-access comparison with established policy, process identity, allowed/denied controls and evidence requirements. Procedure design steps 1-6 present. No target execution requested.
  - requirement:human_file_subject – draft refers to “Object under test identified with stable path/identifier” d64288cb04697:b9 and “object identifier” d64288cb04697:b36,b57. File objects are not explicitly named as files and the methodology is not made clear to test file read access specifically; object is generic. Advertised conclusion defeated: methodology tests file read access and identifies the file objects being read.

* Technical support
  - Asserted factual mechanisms:
    * “Linux open(2) requires caller have read permission on the object for read access.” d64288cb04697:b37
    * “Linux open(2) documents that the requested access to the file is not allowed when permission is lacking.” d64288cb04697:b43
  - Retained source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html, characters 132, inspected_intervals []. No passages retrieved in this pass. Source support for the exact phrasing “requires that the caller have read permission on the object” and “The requested access to the file is not allowed” cannot be verified from inspected evidence. Selection reason claims support d64288cb04697:m18. Material impact on core:technical_support.

No concrete defect identified in procedure design; limitations note bounded excerpt d64288cb04697:b69.

* Restrictions

1. human_file_subject missing explicit file read access statement and file object identification. Draft references generic object. Need smallest correction to make clear methodology tests file read access and identify the file objects being read.
2. Technical support for open(2) permission requirement and denial semantics is asserted without verifiable retained passages in this inspection. Need source-backed support or remove unsupported factual assertions.
